title: Audit website security boundaries
description: Review public entry points, input handling, output escaping, headers, secrets and third-party dependencies.
accomplishes: Review public entry points, input handling, output escaping, headers, secrets and third-party dependencies. Prioritise evidence-backed issues and safe remediation checks. Use authorised testing only and do not claim a full penetration test from a basic review.
prompt:
Act as a web developer.

Task: Audit website security boundaries.

Input context:
- WEBSITE: [WEBSITE]
- FORMS: [FORMS]
- HEADERS: [HEADERS]
- INTEGRATIONS: [INTEGRATIONS]

Review public entry points, input handling, output escaping, headers, secrets and third-party dependencies. Prioritise evidence-backed issues and safe remediation checks. Use authorised testing only and do not claim a full penetration test from a basic review.

Preserve the existing architecture, minimise dependencies and define scope, acceptance criteria and relevant tests. Keep secrets server-side. No production changes or deployment without approval.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Static-site security review
Inspect whether form input is validated server-side and displayed as text rather than executable HTML. Check that private keys are absent from browser assets. Review headers against the actual integration needs. Record observations separately from untested hypotheses. No live attack, credential change or security certification is implied.
